title: Augmenting Clinical Workflow With a Structured Chatbot for Patient History Collection and Diagnostic Support
official: Prospective Observational Evaluation of a Structured, Agentic AI Chatbot for Pre-Visit Patient History Collection and Diagnostic Support in Outpatient Clinical Workflows
summary: Doctors spend much of each visit collecting the patient's medical history, and incomplete histories can delay diagnosis. This study tests an AI chatbot that interviews patients before their appointment and produces a structured summary of their history for the doctor. Adult patients at the first study site, a university gynecology outpatient clinic in Germany, answer the chatbot's questions on a tablet before the doctor visit. The doctor then takes the history and examines the patient as usual, without seeing the chatbot's output. Only after the doctor has finished planning care does the doctor review the chatbot's summary and rate its usefulness and accuracy. The chatbot does not change patient care. Patients also rate the ease of use and acceptability of the chatbot. The investigators will report how useful doctors find the summaries, how complete and correct the summaries are, and how patients experience the tool.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Women 18 years or older

First presentation or new complaint at the gynecology outpatient clinic (self-presentation, emergency, or referral)

Sufficient German language skills to complete a structured patient interview independently

Able to complete study participation without external support

Written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

Acute emergency requiring immediate treatment (for example, impaired consciousness, hemodynamic instability, or acute bleeding requiring immediate care)

Lack of legal or decisional capacity to consent

Insufficient language skills

Severe cognitive, visual, or motor impairment preventing tablet use

Previous participation in this study

Refusal or withdrawal of consent
